races.name: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed)

runners_data.name: Gomez Addams
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1-5-1, three runs on Good) and De Bromhead/O'Keeffe combination is solid, but this horse races prominently by nature and with four rivals competing for that band it is likely to find itself further back than ideal, which tempers its chance in a shape favouring position.|

runners_data.name: Magico
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins and brings serious jockey quality, but Magico's best recent form on Good (5th and 6th at 16f) and only one win from nine Good-ground starts makes this a harder sell at OR 120; will look to race prominently but faces stiff competition for that position.|

runners_data.name: Porcupine Bank
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 130, has won two of three starts on Good ground at 16f and Sam Ewing has been in decent form for Elliott; prominent style suits this field shape well and it has the class to make its position count when the pace quickens from three out.|

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up horse with credible form — a recent second over 20f on Good (2/20f/GOO) is the standout run — and tongue-tie is noted; most likely to benefit if the pace collapses, but is otherwise dependent on a scenario that this race shape does not strongly favour.|

runners_data.name: Bruise Hill
runners_data.note: Consistent record of fading in the finish (form 9080-6) and all four recent runs on Good have returned poor positions; no wins or placings on Good ground and the OR of 82 makes this hard to recommend in any scenario against this class of opposition.|

runners_data.name: Lizzie Twigg
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy aboard, OR 127, and a remarkable record of three wins from four starts on Good ground at 16f for Elliott — form 1-5-1-1 in those conditions is the best Going-specific profile in this race; prominent style fits perfectly in this congested field if it secures a clean position behind Fastnet Crystal.|

runners_data.name: Milan Forth
runners_data.note: Ran just four days ago (LR:4d) which is a notable flag in a race of this quality, and all five recent runs have been over 20f on Good or Yielding, suggesting the drop back to 2m½f is a slight query; tongue-tie worn, and while prominent style fits the shape it may lack freshness at the business end.|

runners_data.name: Fastnet Crystal
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, which gives J J Slevin full control of the race from the outset; one win from three starts (1/18f/GOO) with a second on Soft, trained by the in-form Joseph Patrick O'Brien (T14: 19/64), and the ability to dictate a sustainable pace on Good ground is this horse's primary tactical asset.|

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Five consecutive placed efforts at 16f on Good (two seconds, one third) show admirable consistency but no win from the prominent position it prefers; by nature a prominent racer, this field's overcrowded front ranks make it likely to be shuffled further back than its record suggests it performs best — the style-fit concern is real at OR 120 in Listed company.|

races.paceDynamic: Fastnet Crystal is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, J J Slevin can dictate terms at a measured gallop on Good ground, setting a comfortable pace through the early stages of this 2m½f trip. The prominent group is heavily congested — Magico, Porcupine Bank, Lizzie Twigg, and Milan Forth all want to race close to the pace, meaning a scrappy early jostle for position behind Fastnet Crystal is likely, with real traffic risk approaching the third-last. Gomez Addams and Brave Lady are both natural prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their preferred berth in this shape, so they will find themselves further back than ideal, which blunts their chance in any scenario that rewards horses racing prominently from the outset. This race shape — an uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable pace, followed by a compact prominent pack — strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can travel smoothly in second or third without burning energy, and who possess enough class to quicken when Fastnet Crystal is challenged from two out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fastnet Crystal Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Fastnet Crystal retains the lead unchallenged and the prominent pack behind fail to close the gap decisively from two out.
scenarios.body: Slevin dictates a fair but undemanding gallop, conserves plenty for the final two hurdles, and Fastnet Crystal's course form (1/18f/GOO) suggests it handles this track well at this trip; the horse can quicken clear when asked if rivals have burned energy scrapping for position behind it. Horses who travel fluently in the chasing group — particularly those with class to match — are best placed to challenge, but the leader's advantage of racing in rhythm throughout is significant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fastnet Crystal's gallop is just quick enough to string the field out and one prominent horse tracks it perfectly to lead at the last.
scenarios.body: A settled, well-positioned horse travelling smoothly off the leader's shoulder is ideally placed as the race begins in earnest from three out; Lizzie Twigg (3 wins from 4 starts on Good, Jack Kennedy aboard) or Porcupine Bank (OR 130, two wins on Good) are the most natural beneficiaries of this shape given their form and position. The prominent congestion behind means the horse who avoids early traffic and finds clean air from the second-last wins the tactical battle as much as the physical one.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack pushes Fastnet Crystal into an unsustainably quick gallop early on and the race falls apart from three out.
scenarios.body: With four horses wanting to race close to the pace and all of them jostling for position, it is possible the early tempo becomes more pressured than Fastnet Crystal's connections intend, leaving the leader and prominent horses tired late; this would theoretically open the door for hold-up types, but Brosna Town (best recent form 2/20f/GOO) is the only genuine hold-up runner with credible form. Even in this shape, the redistribution of Gomez Addams and Brave Lady into the midfield band means the true closers are limited in number and class.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horses Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a muddling pace that compresses the field and produces a mass finish from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race would allow Milan Forth and Gomez Addams, both racing further back than they would like, to get competitive late if they pick up ground through tired horses; however, Milan Forth ran only four days ago and carries the wear of a recent run, while Gomez Addams is out of its natural role. This scenario is the least likely given the clear front-runner and the incentive for prominent horses to press on from three out.

watchPoints.text: Fastnet Crystal — if J J Slevin establishes a clear lead unchallenged from the outset, the horse can control tempo and has a significant tactical advantage over a field with no natural challenger for the front; watch whether the prominent pack attempt to close the gap early.

Traffic danger between the 3rd-last and 2nd-last hurdle — with Magico, Porcupine Bank, Lizzie Twigg, and Milan Forth all fighting for the same prominent positions, expect bumping or tightening as the race begins in earnest; horses caught flat-footed here could lose all chance.
Milan Forth — ran only four days ago and faces a significant freshness concern in a Listed race; watch whether it travels with its usual fluency or begins to drop away before two out.

Gomez Addams and Brave Lady — both natural prominent racers likely to be racing out of role in midfield; if either manages to find an unexpectedly clean passage and reach their natural position, the race shape changes, but the probability of both securing it is low given the congestion ahead of them.

Bruise Hill — consistent pattern of fading late across all four recent Good-ground runs; if prominent early, watch for it to weaken from three out and potentially interfere with runners attempting to challenge on the inner.

races.name: Latin Quarter Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Arch Empire
runners_data.note: The one genuine hold-up horse in the field; Gordon Elliott handler with a consistent recent profile (form 497-68), has run five times on Good and shown modest placed returns — needs the pace to be genuine and sustained to deliver his late effort, which is not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Begger
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged as such, with only two runs recorded on similar going and both finishing positions unavailable — William Harvey yard at 0/4 in the last 14 days and 72 days off adds layers of unknown; the U (unseated) interrupts an already thin profile and this trip/track combination is a real step into the unknown.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partnership for Gordon Elliott is high-profile, and this horse has won twice on Good including a Heathfield win — importantly, he is a natural front-runner who will be looking to press forward but, with prominent positions at a premium, he may find himself racing closer to the rear than his two hurdle wins suggest he wants.

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins aboard for the powerful Mullins yard (4/19 in 14 days), and this horse has a placed effort at 23f on Good plus a Listed-grade hurdle placing — the tongue-tie is noted, and his 0PP-38 form shows inconsistency but he has genuine claims as a natural prominent runner who should secure a position close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Frankie John
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan runner who returned a win at 20f on Good and placed twice at the same trip — his natural style is genuinely prominent but the crowded front end means Daniel King will likely be squeezed back to midfield, a role that does not maximise his strengths; 90 days off since last run is a query.

runners_data.name: Great Attitude
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 130 and the lone confirmed front-runner — Ricky Doyle can dictate entirely on his own terms from the off; only three runs on record and just 1/3 on similar going, but the class edge and pace control give him a structural advantage that the field cannot easily counteract.

runners_data.name: Love Me Tender
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for W P Mullins on a mare with three wins from seven on Good ground and a strong recent record at this sort of trip — she is a natural front-runner at heart but cannot get to the front in this shape, and Cobden will need to manage her back in the pack, a role her form suggests she handles less naturally than racing handy.

runners_data.name: My Great Mate
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's booking for Mullins is significant, and this horse has four placed efforts in 13 runs on Good — but a 323-day absence is the dominant concern, and while his genuine prominent style would suit if he could lead, the crowded pace map means he will be racing in an unfamiliar tracking position on what is effectively a comeback run.

runners_data.name: Robbies Rock
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell-trained five-year-old with three wins from 15 on Good and a recent second at 17f — the tongue-tie is worn, jockey Keith Donoghue brings experience, and with form showing a good run two back at 17f on Good this trip looks within range; as a natural prominent horse he should get a forward berth without the congestion affecting others.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: Peter Smithers claiming 7lbs for David Harry Kelly, who has gone 1/8 in 14 days — ran just six days ago which raises a fitness/freshness query, and his form string (6-972U) with an unseating and a run at 24f on Good suggesting he stays but lacks the sharp form to threaten; the tongue-tie is worn and he has placed at 16f on Good before.

runners_data.name: Jolie Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's OR-114 runner, lowest-rated in the field, with Phillip Enright up — has placed seven times from 15 similar-going runs and finished second at 20f on Good last time, showing she handles this sort of track and trip; another natural front-runner pushed back by the prominent traffic jam, she will need to adapt her approach in a field where she is already conceding class.

races.paceDynamic: Great Attitude is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Ricky Doyle can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m2f trip on Good ground at Galway — a classic uncontested lead scenario that sets up precisely for the horse in front. Behind him, Eclipse Chaser and Robbies Rock are the most naturally prominent types likely to secure the positions closest to the pace, with Bowensonfire also a genuine front-runner who should track the leader from an early stage. This field is overloaded with prominent-running types: My Great Mate, Love Me Tender, Frankie John, and Jolie Jewel are all natural front-to-midfield horses who cannot all get their preferred berths, meaning several will race in unfamiliar, deeper positions than suits them. With the pace honest but uncontested, the tactical picture strongly favours horses that can travel prominently just off Great Attitude and sustain their effort into the final obstacles — patient hold-up types will have ground to make up from a long way out on what is a fair, non-extreme gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Great Attitude travels comfortably in front and no rival has the pace or inclination to challenge for the lead from the off.
scenarios.body: Great Attitude sets a measured tempo, controls the race from the front, and the proximity of Eclipse Chaser or Robbies Rock to the pace gives them first run on the field approaching the final fences; the uncontested gallop means the leader and closest trackers are never emptied out early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Great Attitude weakens from the front in the closing stages and a close-tracking prominent type swoops to take over.
scenarios.body: A horse like Robbies Rock or Bowensonfire, travelling smoothly just off the leader, picks up the pieces when Great Attitude's effort flattens on the run to the last; the Good ground rewards a horse that has conserved energy in a steady early gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Mid-Race Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens unexpectedly mid-race, compressing the field and allowing a well-handicapped midfield mover to weave through.
scenarios.body: Frankie John or My Great Mate, despite being pushed wider than ideal by the prominent logjam, find daylight on the final circuit and arrive with a sustained run from the back of the main group; their natural forward-going style, even if forced to settle, gives them finishing impetus on a sound surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses at the final fence and true hold-up horses benefit from a flat-out finish.
scenarios.body: Arch Empire is the only genuinely natural hold-up horse in the field and would need a strong, searching gallop to set up his late run; this scenario is the least likely given that most apparent hold-up runners are redistributed prominent types who will not produce a true sustained late challenge.

watchPoints.text: Great Attitude sets the entire pace structure — if Ricky Doyle is pressured into going faster than intended in the early stages, the uncontested lead scenario collapses and the race opens up dramatically for the prominent trackers.

The Mullins trio of Eclipse Chaser, Love Me Tender, and My Great Mate create a significant traffic management risk in the early exchanges — watch for crowding around the first few fences as multiple prominent types compete for the same ground.

My Great Mate returns from 323 days off the track — Paul Townend's booking keeps him interesting, but a horse resuming after almost a year over fences on Good ground must be treated with caution regardless of stable confidence.

Bowensonfire at 26 days since last run carries headgear (h) and is a natural front-runner being mapped further back — watch whether Jack Kennedy elects to push forward regardless, which could disrupt Great Attitude's uncontested lead assumption entirely.

Begger (72 days off, lightly raced, trainer 0/4 in 14 days) is the most opaque runner in the field — any market move for this Ben Harvey-ridden unknown in the ring would be worth noting given the paper form tells almost nothing.

races.name: COLM QUINN BMW Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Crescent Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for Gavin Cromwell, ran five times on Good with one win and one place in similar going; 52 days since last run but trainer in fair recent form, and the 6-year-old wears tongue-strap and cheekpieces — needs a strong pace to deliver from off it.

runners_data.name: Fort Randall
runners_data.note: Strong course-distance profile with two wins and four places from ten runs on Good — consistently performs over this trip and has genuine stamina credentials; amateur jockey Mr O McGill carries a 5lb claim which tempers confidence, but the horse's record here is hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will likely lead, but STYLE_FIT flag warns this is out of recent role given form figures suggest a more prominent than front-running tendency; tongue-strap fitted and 28 days fresh — the real question is whether 23 rivals pressure it into going too fast.

runners_data.name: Butter Fingers
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 5-year-old for Ross O'Sullivan who bounced back to win last time on Good going at 16f; stepping up in a big competitive handicap off 82 days, but career-best on this surface and the prominent style suits the race shape perfectly with Shane Markey's 7lb claim a bonus.

runners_data.name: Ned In The Park
runners_data.note: Five of his last five runs have been on Good ground and he handles it reliably; a genuine prominent type who will want to be in the first three or four, and the 20f course form is strong — jockey Mr D Doyle's 7lb claim adds value if the horse can recover from a slight recent run drop-off.

runners_data.name: Finnians Row
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old who has won his last two starts, both on Good over 20f — this course-distance profile is outstanding; tongue bar and blinkers fitted, and the 45-day break is not a concern given Dermot McLoughlin's consistent record; pressing the pace from the front is exactly how this race sets up for him.

runners_data.name: Truckers Cruising
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner has tongue-strap fitted and a trainer who is 3/32 in the last 14 days, but the horse's form on Good going is winless across five tries at this surface — a 1U6-0P recent sequence does not inspire confidence despite the stable form.

runners_data.name: Kilbrin Rocco
runners_data.note: Won two of his last four runs on Good, including last time out over course-distance at 16f; tongue-strap worn and 82-day break is worth a note, but the prominent style and proven good-ground form makes him a live player if freshness is not an issue.

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who showed a placed effort on Soft last time and has recent course form, but the nine-runner index on Good is moderate at 8/14; the 12-day turnaround is quick and the prominent style fits the map, though recent finishes suggest a tendency to underperform late.

runners_data.name: Tell Us This
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good recently and is 16 days fresh, which is ideal; races prominently and the tongue-strap is familiar — the step back up to 18f+ is the only query but the 2W3P record on Good is solid and the position in the race should suit.

runners_data.name: Cahirdown Boy
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old returning from 168 days off, which is a significant fitness concern regardless of ability; his Good-ground figures are modest at 6/15 with no wins, and the long break over an unforgiving Galway test makes this a very risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Drop A Threat
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained hold-up horse who carries tongue-strap, but the form string (74-0P5) is uninspiring and the Good-ground record shows no wins in six attempts on that surface; trainer 4/19 in 14 days provides the only reason to keep onside.

runners_data.name: A Snow White Park
runners_data.note: Consistent young mare with two second-place finishes from her last two starts on Good over 20-22f — the form is rock-solid and the step to this trip is a positive; Danny Mullins takes the ride and the prominent profile should allow her to sit in a good spot.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Patrick Griffin's yard with a fine record of 12 runs on Good (one win, eight places) — rarely far away but rarely wins; the 37-day break is fine and the 6-year-old needs a genuine gallop to get into it from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Giant Haystacks
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Good and is a natural prominent racer — however the field's depth of pace means he has been mapped to midfield as he's unlikely to achieve his preferred position; the STYLE_FIT discount is real, but ability on this surface for Ross O'Sullivan is genuine.

runners_data.name: Driveonwill
runners_data.note: Another Ross O'Sullivan prominent type who has been pushed back on the map due to the same front-rank traffic; won over 20f on Good and comes here 45 days fresh — the redistribution penalty is worth heeding, as racing in the pack rather than on the front end weakens his primary weapon.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's filly is only 6 days since her last run and wears tongue-strap and a hood; her natural style is prominent but with the field stacked with pace she is unlikely to get that position — Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong jockey booking but the redistribution and quick turnaround temper expectations.

runners_data.name: That's About Right
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing tongue-strap and a hood, with a reasonable Good-ground record (13/15) despite no recent wins; P J Rothwell is 2/32 in the last 14 days and the horse has finished fourth or worse in five of its last five — hard to construct a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Consistent and handles Good ground perfectly (15/15 runs on that surface with one win), but her natural instinct is to race forward and she has been mapped back due to overcrowding up front; the strong consistent placed record and young age make her interesting if chaos opens a route, though the position compromise is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Mount Shenshan
runners_data.note: Unclassified style for Thomas Mullins, moderate Good-ground record of 8/15 with no wins; the 45-day break and recent finishing positions (4-5-3-5-6) suggest a solid but uninspiring jumper who is unlikely to trouble the principals at this level.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Only 4 days since his last run which is extremely tight preparation; hold-up profile with a moderate Good-ground record and no wins on that surface — the quick turnaround is the dominant concern and makes this hard to support regardless of any latent ability.

runners_data.name: Stily
runners_data.note: No jockey declared, which is a notable concern at this stage; a natural prominent racer whose position has been pushed back due to the crowded front rank — the 0W5P record on Good suggests consistency without a killer punch, and the jockey situation must be resolved before any assessment is meaningful.

runners_data.name: Max Time
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 72 and flagged for fading in the finish; a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield due to the number of closers, and the STYLE_FIT discount compounds an already weak form profile — the 12-day turnaround adds little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, crucially, is unlikely to be seriously pressured for the lead — this creates a sustainable, controlled gallop from the front that will not burn off the pack early. However, the field is loaded with horses whose natural instinct is to race prominently: Butter Fingers, Ned In The Park, Finnians Row, Kilbrin Rocco, Party President, and Tell Us This all want to be on or near the pace, meaning the early order behind Leave In Secret will be congested and competitive for that prominent berth. Giant Haystacks, Stoneyford Lady, Driveonwill, Sea Of Doubt, and Stily are genuine prominent-running types who are mapped to midfield purely because there is insufficient room for all of them to achieve their natural position — of these, Finnians Row and Ned In The Park, with proven good-ground form and course-distance profiles, are most likely to actually secure a forward position. A controlled pace with a large field at Galway's testing track — where the uphill finish demands stamina — favours horses that race prominently and travel sweetly rather than those trying to make up ground from the rear, making an efficient, well-positioned prominent racer the primary profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent pack tracks efficiently without burning out.
scenarios.body: Leave In Secret dictates a manageable fractions, allowing horses racing in the first four or five to conserve energy before the Galway hill; the congestion behind the leader means those who travel prominently without over-racing hold a decisive positional edge at the second-last. Finnians Row and Ned In The Park, both consistent on Good ground with strong course-distance profiles, are ideally placed to pounce from this position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Sorts It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively demanding despite appearing steady, and the race turns into an endurance slog up the Galway hill.
scenarios.body: A big field on Good ground over 2m2f at Galway naturally stretches horses physically, and any horse carrying weight without a high cruising rate will be exposed; those with genuine stamina and recent winning form over the trip will outlast rivals who flatten out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swings Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set things up for closers and the prominent horses empty approaching the last.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo would thin the prominent pack before the final fence, opening a narrow late-run lane; however, the Galway finish is notoriously punishing for hold-up horses and several horses tagged as hold-up types here are not natural closers pushed off the pace rather than true deep finishers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Big-Field Chaos, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or traffic trouble disrupt the prominent pack and create an unforeseeable outcome.
scenarios.body: In a 23-runner handicap chase, scrimmaging at fences can eliminate or hamper the market leaders, gifting race-fit horses at longer odds a clear passage; Sea Of Doubt and Giant Haystacks, while racing out of their natural prominent role here, retain enough ability to capitalise if the principals are compromised.

watchPoints.text: Finnians Row and Ned In The Park — both will compete aggressively for the prominent positions directly behind Leave In Secret from the off, and any early scrimmaging or jumping incident between these two could compromise the pace map entirely.

Giant Haystacks, Stoneyford Lady, and Driveonwill are all being raced out of their natural prominent roles due to the overcrowded front rank — watch how aggressively their jockeys try to overcome the map in the early stages, as a push for position could inject unexpected pace into the race.

Stily has no jockey declared — if a late or inexperienced replacement is booked, this horse's behaviour at the start and through the field in a 23-runner chase could create traffic problems for those around it.

My Cullen runs just 4 days after his last start — monitor the pre-race paddock closely, as a horse who is below peak fitness in a competitive 23-runner chase on Good ground represents a genuine jumping risk rather than a winning threat.
Leave In Secret carries a STYLE_FIT flag as racing slightly out of role at the head

races.name: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Norwalk Havoc
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for Harrington and Foley, but poor recent form string (0-7830) and limited wins on similar going (0W1P in 5 sim-going runs) give little confidence; 51 days off and tongue-tie applied.

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good ground for Thorne's yard and a big-field winner profile makes him interesting; 3-pound claim from Kearney helps at the weights, and his 10f form suggests stamina won't be an issue here.

runners_data.name: Ribee
runners_data.note: 104 days off is a significant concern for a horse whose only similar-going run produced no wins; trainer Mulvany has sent out three runners in 14 days showing stable activity, and tongue-tie fitted.

runners_data.name: Dunum
runners_data.note: 318 days absent is the headline for this 8-year-old; won over 8f on Good for Lupini previously and has course-going form (1W3P), but that layoff at his age is very hard to forgive in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f at Galway on Good — course form is live and the step up to 1m½f is unproven but not impossible; front-running horses habitually pushed back to prominent role by this busy stable.

runners_data.name: Hardy Warrior
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; O'Brien's three-year-old won over 8f on Soft and has finished close on Good, and with no pacemaking rival he can dictate — his STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) reflects that he is being asked to lead in a more exposed role than usual.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Murphy who has gone 3/5 places in sim-going, but form figures of 863678 don't suggest a horse about to break through in a 21-runner handicap; 19 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Three placed efforts from five for Thorne and Coen on Good ground including two runner-up finishes, making him a solid each-way contender if he can break cleanly and take up his natural prominent position.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at Galway on Good (1/8f, 1/8f) last two starts is a compelling local course-and-distance angle; trainer-jockey combo is the same Slattery combination and recent form (5-211) is frank — must be respected.

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Won at this track on Good (1/8f) and has multiple Good-ground wins; 2W3P from 5 sim-going runs for McGuinness is solid, and a return to Galway after 30 days off puts him firmly in the frame as a prominent runner.

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Most recent run was a second on Good over 8f for Gibney; genuine hold-up horse with decent Good-ground figures (2W4P across 12 runs), but needs a strong tempo set up by the prominent runners ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Orandi
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who wants to race prominently but is pushed into a deeper position by the crowded map; recent form (0-0078) on Good and Heavy is uninspiring, and the true style mismatch tempers enthusiasm despite the redistribution flag.

runners_data.name: Genuine Article
runners_data.note: Dropped from 16f back to this shorter trip, which is a significant class and distance query; though naturally front-running in style, the horse is mapped to midfield due to overcrowding, adding further doubt about finding a clean run.

runners_data.name: Lady Lilac
runners_data.note: Has placed at 10f on Soft and 8f on Heavy for Murphy, and while naturally prominent in style, the sheer volume of similar horses means she's unlikely to secure that position today; gelded headgear (b) noted.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Course-proven with multiple Good-ground near-misses (4P from 5 sim-going runs for Ellison) and genuinely wants to race up with the pace; the congested prominent berths mean Hayes may find himself squeezed wider than ideal, but the ability to hold position gives this one a fighting chance if the map is kinder than expected.

runners_data.name: Terre De Vega
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Kinsella with headgear (hb) applied; one win at 8f on Heavy for this trip range, but only 3 from 8 in similar going and laid-off 46 days — needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Howyoulikethat
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old for McLoughlin who has placed on Good (3/8f) most recently; hold-up style dependent on pace being strong, and with Burns on a 5lb claim this is a long-shot angle in an open handicap.

runners_data.name: Kai Lung
runners_data.note: Mullins runner whose last five runs have been over 16f — the drop to 1m½f is an enormous trip reduction and his genuine prominent style is blocked by the overcrowded map; experience over shorter trips is the glaring gap.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Two wins at 10f and 12f on Good for Cody are recent and relevant; true hold-up horse mapped to midfield through redistribution — needs a strong pace, and while form is solid, style mismatch is a drag on raw expectations.

runners_data.name: Monvoe
runners_data.note: Three wins from five Good-ground runs for Cody including back-to-back victories; a 3-year-old who naturally wants to be prominent but is squeezed out of position in this 21-runner field — the talent is genuine, the position is the problem.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Jardine's 3-year-old has placed twice on Good including a third at 8f; hold-up performer with a modest sim-going record who is running off a likely advantageous mark if everything sets up — needs pace and a clear passage.

races.paceDynamic: Hardy Warrior is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no identified rival pressing for the lead, should be able to slot into a comfortable, uncontested gallop — sustainable rather than blistering on Good ground over 1m½f. The field is loaded with prominent-types who will fan out behind him: Loughrea, Pierre Royal, Jagged Edge, Gleneagle Bay and Far From Dandy all want to race up close, but with only one legitimate lead position available, several of them — including Lir Speciale, Orandi, Kai Lung, Monvoe and Lady Lilac — will be forced wider and deeper than they'd like, effectively racing out of role. That congestion in the prominent berths means the pace is unlikely to be truly strong, and a steady-to-fair tempo set by Hardy Warrior will compress the field, limiting how much ground hold-up horses can make up in the straight. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race handily in second or third, travelling within themselves before pressing Hardy Warrior in the final two furlongs — genuine prominent types with good figures on Good ground are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hardy Warrior Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior settles into an uncontested lead and the pace is steady enough that he has fuel left entering the Galway straight.
scenarios.body: Hardy Warrior dictates throughout at a fair clip, and those tracking him closely — Loughrea and Pierre Royal — are the primary beneficiaries if the front-runner is run down; if he is not, Hardy Warrior wins outright from his ideal lead position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the sheer volume of prominent-runners forces a stronger pace than Hardy Warrior intends, and the front-runner is spent entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The surge of Loughrea, Pierre Royal and Far From Dandy in behind Hardy Warrior creates more pressure than he bargained for, and one of the horses tracking in the first three overtakes him inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to burn off the prominent horses and the hold-up brigade gets a clear run up the straight.
scenarios.body: Booyea and Norwalk Havoc, tracking from off the pace, need a genuine gallop to get into the race — if the prominent scrum produces a true pace, they can pick off tired rivals in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If several of the true prominent horses — Lir Speciale, Monvoe or Kai Lung — successfully carve out better positions than their mapped role suggests and outrun the market.
scenarios.body: Despite being forced wider than ideal, a horse like Lir Speciale (course-proven on Good) or Monvoe (in-form and lightly campaigned at 3) finds a position just off the pace and delivers a late prominent challenge.

watchPoints.text: Loughrea has won his last two at this exact track and trip on Good ground — if Andrew Slattery claims a clean early position just behind Hardy Warrior, this horse is the biggest danger to the front-runner.
Pierre Royal has won at Galway on Good and is 2W3P on this surface — watch him track the leader in second or third and challenge from the two-furlong pole.

Hardy Warrior must break cleanly and secure the lead unchallenged in the first two furlongs; if Far From Dandy, Jagged Edge or Loughrea push for the front, the pace lifts and Hardy Warrior's stamina at 1m½f becomes a serious question.

With 21 runners and a field packed with prominent types, the first bend will be congested — horses like Monvoe, Kai Lung and Lir Speciale who are forced wide could lose several lengths before the race settles, effectively removing them from contention.

Booyea's most recent run was a second on Good over 8f — if the pace turns genuinely strong due to the prominent traffic jam, he is a hold-up horse worth monitoring as a place finisher in the closing stages.

races.name: caulfieldindustrial.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Sommelier
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Kieran Cotter, but flagged as fading in the finish — that warning tempers expectations significantly over 7f on Good; last win came over 6f on Good (14 runs ago) and this trip may just stretch him.

runners_data.name: It'sneverjustone
runners_data.note: David Loughnane runner who hasn't raced in 44 days; placed once from seven attempts on Good, and six attempts over 7f show a level but uninspiring profile with no win at this trip.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness eight-year-old who ran just 10 days ago and has placed on Good ground three times recently over shorter trips; the step up to 7f from his usual 6f pitch is a query but he has course form.

runners_data.name: Vlhova
runners_data.note: Gerard O'Leary's four-year-old is the race's lone front-runner and will likely get a soft lead — however she is tagged as racing out of her most natural role at this shorter trip, and her best form has come at 8f-10f on Good-to-Soft.

runners_data.name: Dragon Of Malta
runners_data.note: P F O'Donnell's nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose true running style is at the rear of the field, though he appears in midfield here simply because the map has no room for more closers; 48 days off the track and mixed form on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Great Mover
runners_data.note: W McCreery's prominent racer has placed twice from 18 attempts on Good, usually at 9f-10f — stepping down to 7f on faster ground is an untested profile and the trip looks sharp.

runners_data.name: Inishfallen
runners_data.note: Stephen Thorne's five-year-old holds two places from nine Good-ground runs and has consistent recent form at 6f; the step up to 7f for the first time is the key question, though his style of racing just off the pace suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Mehman
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes the ride on this seven-year-old who has placed at 7f on Good before; only three runs on similar going across 15 attempts is a small sample but his hold-up style could work if a clean passage materialises through the big field.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan runner who raced 10 days ago; genuinely a hold-up horse by nature, though the overcrowded rear of the field means he is shown in midfield — his best run was a second over 6f on Good and the extra furlong is untested territory.

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this five-year-old for Adrian McGuinness — won over 7f on Good and placed twice at this trip, making him one of the most course-and-distance relevant horses; ran six days ago but the quick turnaround hasn't stopped this yard before.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Second McGuinness runner alongside Eddie G — won twice over 7f including on Good ground, and placed at this trip on Soft; the trainer having three runners here could complicate tactics, but this horse's 7f Good record is among the strongest in the race.

runners_data.name: Heliogabalus
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this Shane Byrne five-year-old who has won twice on Good ground over 8f — stepping back to 7f is a potential positive, and his strike rate in similar conditions (12 from 15 runs on Good) is the most impressive going-relevance figure in the field.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Gillian Scott's five-year-old ran just three days ago and is a natural hold-up horse displaced into midfield by the crowded rear; his one win came over 8f on Soft and Good form has yielded only one placing from 10 attempts.

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: Noel Kelly's nine-year-old is a proven hold-up specialist who has won twice and placed five times over 7f — the race shape compression forces him into a midfield map position that is not his natural home, which is the key discount against his otherwise solid form figures at this trip.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination of Andrew Slattery is notable; the four-year-old has placed six times from 12 runs on Good over 8f but all recent form is over a mile — dropping to 7f is a new test and the prominent style should see him well-placed at least.

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: Reserve 1 for Evanna McCutcheon; has placed twice from 11 Good-ground runs including a second over 7f on Good and a second over 7f on Soft — if he takes his place he is a consistent, genuine contender from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Peter Lawlor's six-year-old is a true hold-up horse by nature whose recent form (four finishes of 5th or worse) gives little encouragement; the redistribution into midfield on the map does not change the fact that his current form is modest.

runners_data.name: Banner Beauty
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's four-year-old has form figures of 00 in the last two runs and showed a win on Good ground only from a small sample eight runs ago — a natural closer mapped into midfield by necessity, with nothing in recent form to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Vlhova is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 7f handicap at Galway and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead, she should secure an uncontested rail position and dictate a sustainable, honest gallop rather than a frenetic pace. Behind her, Eddie G, Goal Exceeded, Great Mover, Heliogabalus, Zaraahmando and Send Harry all seek prominent positions, meaning the prominent berths will be fiercely contested in the opening furlong and several of these will have to settle deeper than ideal. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Dragon Of Malta, Alfred Tennyson, Shoot To Kill, Red Hugh O'Donnell, Summer Snow and Banner Beauty are all genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield in the shape, meaning the true backmarkers will be racing out of their natural groove entirely. With one controlled pace-setter and a moderately honest gallop expected, the race shape favours horses who can race prominently just off Vlhova and produce a sustained finish — prominent-to-midfield types who handle Good ground and have course-relevant form carry the structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vlhova Leads, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Vlhova makes all or near-all at a controlled tempo and one of the prominent chasers can track closely and power past inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Vlhova sets a genuine but manageable pace, leaving just enough for the horse immediately behind to collar her late; the controlled gallop means stamina is less of a premium than a clean passage and a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Rapier Thrust
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough early that the genuine midfield runners pick up powerfully in the straight to overhaul the prominent horses.
scenarios.body: Horses like Mehman, Inishfallen and Go Athletico who settle in mid-division benefit if the pace is honest enough to stop the leaders from conserving energy; a clean run through a packed 18-horse field on Good ground becomes the key.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closers Outstay Field
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens sharply enough in the middle third to string out the field, allowing horses held up at the rear to deliver a sweeping late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally discounted because several horses tagged as true hold-up types have been redistributed into midfield rather than the rear, meaning authentic late finishers are fewer than they appear; Sommelier is the most genuine closer in the field but is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 18-runner field produces significant traffic problems, interference or a false pace that fragments the race into multiple groups.
scenarios.body: A breakout outcome where a horse with a clean passage from a low draw and a prominent position benefits disproportionately from the bunching that often occurs over 7f at Galway with big fields; Heliogabalus, who has a strong record on Good ground, would be well-positioned to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Eddie G and Goal Exceeded are trained by the same handler (Adrian McGuinness, who also runs Go Athletico) — watch for possible team tactics where one acts as pacemaker or sacrificial rabbit to suit the stable's preferred runner, potentially distorting the race shape beyond Vlhova's lead.

With 18 runners over 7f at Galway, the opening two furlongs will see aggressive jostling for prominent berths — horses drawn wide (particularly those with high stall numbers) risk being shuffled back early, radically altering their chance regardless of form.

Vlhova's pace is described as sustainable and uncontested, but she is rated a style-fit concern at this trip — if she weakens suddenly in the straight rather than being overtaken in a controlled fashion, it could cause interference and a chaotic final two furlongs.

Several horses returning on a short turnaround (Eddie G 6 days, Alfred Tennyson and Go Athletico both 10 days) — watch market moves at the off for any signs of market support or drifts that suggest stable confidence or fitness concern.

Heliogabalus has the best strike rate on Good ground in the race (12 from 15 qualifying runs) — if Shane Foley can position him prominently without being drawn into covering too much ground early, he becomes a structural fit for the dominant race shape.

races.name: Caulfield Industrial Handicap

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Good-ground form (sim-going 8/15) who has placed once at this track; trainer William Harvey has had no winners in the past 14 days from 4 runs and needs a stronger pace than Java Wood is likely to set to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Consistent fader whose form string of 800000 tells its own story; Chris Hayes cannot manufacture a finish for a horse that has not placed in six straight runs, and the 10-furlong form is not replicated at this shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for R P Burns with a clean Good-ground profile but a record of placing nowhere in similar fields at Galway; Nicola Burns claims five pounds but the form (25th and 15th recently) gives little traction even at a reasonable weight.

runners_data.name: Java Wood
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner who last won over this exact course and distance combination; the 46-day break is a question mark but Browne McMonagle is an elite handler of pace and the note tagging this horse as racing out of role refers to its occasionally prominent rather than fully front-running profile — here it will lead by default and that is the key tactical fact.

runners_data.name: San Aer
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type for Ross O'Sullivan who has tongue-tie and a poor recent record (17th, 11th, 14th in similar fields); the eight-year-old needs everything to go right from a wide draw in a field this large.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse that won over 10f on Good at Galway and placed at 12f; Shane Foley gives this a significant jockey upgrade and the step back in trip from its most recent runs could be a concern, but its finishing profile is one of the better late options.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good heart after winning at Galway over 8f on Good last time; Ben Coen takes the ride for Ciaran Murphy whose yard has had a winner in the past 14 days, and the horse's two wins from 14 Good-ground starts underline its affinity for conditions today.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose best form has come over longer trips (10-13f on Good/Sta); stepping back to this distance for Robbie Colgan and Matthew J Smith, there is a question whether the pace will be strong enough to flatten out the field and play to her staying strengths.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a win over 7f on Good at Galway last time and consistent Good-ground figures (11/15 runs); the 7-pound claiming apprentice is a slight concern in a competitive handicap, but the horse's course form is genuine and Andrew Slattery's yard is in strong form (5/32 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Finsceal Annie
runners_data.note: Prominent type who carries headgear (tp) and has struggled in similar fields, not placing in her last five runs on Good; Ciaran Murphy's second runner today and the 19-day break has not obviously freshened her form.

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 8f on Good at Galway and has a clear preference for the track; Jimmy Dalton claims 7lbs and while the rider is inexperienced at this level, the horse's track record and Good-ground figures (4/15 runs but 1 win) make it a live each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Lady Arwen
runners_data.note: Won twice recently (10f and 8f on Good and Soft) and is trained by the in-form Conor O'Dwyer (3/4 in 14 days); mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with hold-up types, meaning she may not get the late run her style demands — W J Lee will need to be creative with positioning.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type (10 years old) with four placings in five runs over 7-10f on Good; mapped to midfield against its natural style because the field's hold-up contingent is outsized, and at OR 68 the weight is not prohibitive but the horse's age works against it in a sharp-finish scenario.

runners_data.name: Rhythm King
runners_data.note: Has not run for 274 days and all five recent runs are on Heavy/Soft at Dundalk or Good at Galway with no wins in that period; the layoff is the defining concern and Good form (only 2/15 runs historically) does not inspire confidence on return.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent type with the best Good-ground run profile in the field (12/15), including two wins and five places from 8f-10f Good; Sam Coen claims 5lbs and the horse finished 2nd last time over 8f Good, making this a strong each-way contender if it can hold its prominent position.

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Hold-up type mapped to midfield because of field congestion at the rear; best form has come over 8f on Good (two 5ths) and the 32-day break for Denis Hogan's yard (3/26 in 14 days) is not alarming, but the step back from longer trips and the style mismatch reduce confidence.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and placed twice in Good-ground sprints; mapped to midfield rather than the rear because true hold-up horses outnumber available positions, meaning Paul Flynn's runner may not get the strong pace it needs — the headgear (t) and 13-day freshener are positives.

runners_data.name: Queen Aethelflaed
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over 8f on Good at Galway and finished 2nd at 8f on Good — an excellent course-and-distance profile; Orla Tynan claims 7lbs which softens the weight, and Andrew Slattery's yard in excellent form (5/32) means the trainer angle is a genuine plus.

runners_data.name: Elusive Duke
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose five-run recent string shows four placings (2nd, 2nd, 2nd, 2nd) at 9-11f on Good — high consistency without winning; pushed into the midfield map position because prominent berths are oversubscribed, so the horse would need to find a way forward from a tracking role that does not suit, tempering its chances.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back over 8f on Good (Galway-track win included) and placed at 7f on Soft; a genuinely prominent racer with the best recent winning form in the field, but forced into a midfield mapping because the prominent group is overloaded — Adrian McGuinness (3/28 in 14 days) and the horse's raw ability make it the most dangerous of the displaced contingent.

runners_data.name: Ballymagreehan
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and finished 7th twice on Good in similar company; a true prominent type for David Marnane (2/19 in 14 days) who will find it difficult to get its natural travelling position given the crowd ahead — the style mismatch is the primary obstacle to its chances today.

races.paceDynamic: Java Wood is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle, will stride forward from the gate and control this 1m½f contest on Good ground at Galway at a sustainable, uncontested gallop — not a punishing tempo. Behind him, Bay Of Dreams, Cala Bonita, Faoladh, Finsceal Annie, Kitty Bear, Bucaneer's Spirit and Queen Aethelflaed are all genuine prominent types who will compete fiercely for the positions immediately behind the leader, creating a compressed and competitive middle section of the field. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can realistically hold those positions: Minaun View, Elusive Duke and Ballymagreehan are true prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled back into midfield against their will, while multiple hold-up horses have been redistributed forward because the rear is over-subscribed. With a single horse able to dictate a measured pace and a bunched chasing pack unable to exert sustained pressure, this race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently in the slipstream of Java Wood and produce a decisive burst in the final two furlongs — the prominent-to-lead profile is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Java Wood Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Java Wood is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the prominent pack burns each other out disputing second.
scenarios.body: Java Wood dictates a measured gallop on Good ground and, never headed, kicks again when challenged in the straight to hold on; with Browne McMonagle managing the fractions expertly, no single pursuer has enough left to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the genuine prominent types settles just off Java Wood's pace and produces a smooth run to the front inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Bay Of Dreams or Queen Aethelflaed, having tracked the leader at a comfortable clip, finds the most for pressure as the race quickens and outstays the front-runner; this suits horses with Good-ground form at this trip who have the tactical speed to switch off and accelerate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Displaced Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Minaun View, Elusive Duke or Ballymagreehan overcomes their forced midfield position and produces a sustained late run on the heels of the leaders.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural position, these horses would need the pace to collapse slightly in the final stages to allow them to motor through; Minaun View's recent back-to-back wins and consistent Good-ground form make her the most likely of the three to pull this off despite the style mismatch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack press Java Wood hard enough to burn the race up, opening the door for genuine hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Blues Emperor, Showyoutheropes or Lady Arwen would need an unusually strong pace — unlikely given Java Wood's uncontested lead — to reel in the leaders; the thin historical basis for a truly pressured tempo here makes this the least probable shape.

watchPoints.text: Java Wood's gallop in the first three furlongs is the race's pivotal moment — if Browne McMonagle sets a genuinely comfortable pace, the race becomes a procession for front-runners and prominent trackers; watch whether any of Bay Of Dreams or Bucaneer's Spirit press him early.

Minaun View, Elusive Duke and Ballymagreehan are all natural prominent racers who will be fighting for fewer positions than exist — watch for shuffling, bumping or traffic issues in the first two furlongs as these horses struggle to find their rhythm.

Queen Aethelflaed and Kitty Bear both carry apprentice riders (Orla Tynan 7lbs, Jimmy Dalton 7lbs) in a 21-runner handicap at Galway — positional errors or lack of experience in a bunched field could compromise both horses' chances regardless of ability.

Lady Arwen's connections (Conor O'Dwyer, 3 winners from 4 in 14 days) are in a red-hot vein of form; watch whether W J Lee attempts to position her closer than her natural hold-up style would suggest, given she cannot rely on a truly strong pace to finish through.

Rhythm King reappears after a 274-day absence — watch its market moves in the final hour before post time as any significant support would suggest the stable has it ready, while drifting odds would confirm the layoff is a genuine concern.
